resources.string: Offline quick reference. Save the route and map before leaving coverage.
Stop moving blindly. Mark your current position, compare it with the route, return only along a clearly known safe segment. If terrain is dangerous, stay in a visible sheltered place.
Do not force movement with a suspected fracture, head injury, severe bleeding or chest pain. Keep the person warm, control bleeding with direct pressure and prepare coordinates for rescuers.
Add dry layers early, protect from wind and rain, avoid exposed ridges during thunderstorms, and turn back before exhaustion. Wet clothing and wind can cool a person quickly even above freezing.
Call 112 whenever any network is available. The SOS card below contains the latest location known to AreaMap and can be copied or shared.

Short route: carry normal water reserve, a charged phone and a wind layer.
Long route: take extra water/food, a power bank, headlamp and leave a time reserve for the return.
Large ascent: take a warm layer, wind/rain protection, extra food and start earlier.
Above 2500 m: expect colder/windier conditions and watch for altitude illness; do not keep ascending if symptoms worsen.
Steep sections detected: be especially careful on descents, wet ground, scree and when tired.
Part of the route is expected to be in darkness: a headlamp is essential; start earlier or shorten the route.
First aid does not replace medical care. For life-threatening emergencies call 112 as soon as any network is available.
